summary: DOMVUS Phase 3 (Operations) — end-to-end test. Backend: 18/18 pytest passing in /app/backend/tests/test_domvus_ops.py covering all 14 scenarios: (1) Occurrence lifecycle create → list → detail (timeline+comments+documents) → add comment → PUT in_progress records status_history → assign supplier+actual_cost → PUT resolved → POST /create-expense creates expense in db.expenses with correct amount and links back via occurrence_id. (2) Maintenance: create annual with next_date, POST /complete sets last_date and recalculates next_date to ~365 days (asserted 360-370) with status back to 'scheduled'; maintenance with past next_date returns status 'overdue'. (3) Contracts: end_date +400d → 'active', +45d → 'expiring', -30d → 'expired'; dashboard contracts_expiring reflects these. (4) Documents: multipart PDF upload succeeds, list, download returns application/pdf bytes starting with %PDF; executable content-type rejected (400). (5) Document security (CRITICAL): owner condomino@ receives 403 downloading a document belonging to another condominium. (6) Communication templates GET returns 4+ defaults; POST send with target_type=condominium resolves owners of that condo, recipient_count>0, status='sent', appears in list, creates in-app notifications for owner users. (7) Assemblies: created with 2 agenda items → agenda numbered 1,2; GET detail returns attendees[]; POST attendee persists (verified length=1). (8) Tasks: create → status 'todo', PUT status='completed' logs activity; mine=true filter returns only tasks assigned to current user. (9) Notifications: GET returns {items, unread}; POST /read-all sets unread=0. (10) Activities: entries returned scoped to condominium, actions include create/status/complete/send/upload. (11) Ops dashboard: all 9 keys returned (open_occurrences, urgent_occurrences, overdue_maintenance, upcoming_maintenance, contracts_expiring, pending_tasks, upcoming_assemblies, recent_communications, recent_activity). (12) Supplier profile / global search: /ops/search?q=TEST_ returns categorized results. (13) TENANT ISOLATION (CRITICAL): owner GET /ops/occurrences is limited to own condominium_id (verified per-row); owner receives 401/403 on POST maintenance/contracts/tasks/communications/documents; owner cannot GET another condo's occurrence detail (403/404). (14) REGRESSION: auth login super_admin/gestor/condomino all pass; /finance/dashboard, /condominiums, /fractions, /owners all 200; Phase 2 finance suite still 12/12 passing (test_domvus_finance.py). Frontend (super_admin master.marques@): Dashboard shows ops-cards + notif-bell; all 7 nav testids present (nav-ocorrencias, nav-manutencao, nav-contratos, nav-comunicacoes, nav-assembleias, nav-tarefas, nav-documentos); Ocorrências list has 23 rows, occ-row click → detail with all 7 detail testids (occ-edit-status/supplier/cost, occ-save, occ-create-expense, comment-input, comment-submit); notif dropdown shows notifications from ops actions. Each ops page renders its add/action button (add-maintenance-btn, add-contract-btn, compose-btn, add-assembly-btn, upload-doc-btn, add-task-btn, my-tasks-toggle). Owner (condomino@): sidebar correctly limited to Dashboard + Minha Conta + Ocorrências + Documentos (nav-manutencao/contratos/tarefas/comunicacoes/assembleias/financas/fornecedores all HIDDEN); ops KPIs on the owner Dashboard are scoped to their own condominium.

issues: Multiple 'ResponsiveContainer width(-1) height(-1)' console warnings on first render — cosmetic, resolves once layout stabilises.

Dropdown open state adds an invisible overlay on <html> that intercepts sidebar clicks; users must click outside to dismiss it before navigating. Consider setting pointer-events:none on the popover backdrop or closing on nav click.

critical_code_review_comments: operations.py list_occurrences (line 118-126) — unused variable 'frac' fetched inside the ROLE_OWNER branch and never used to filter results; the ROLE_OWNER owner-scope check is effectively bypassed for occurrences with a fraction_id belonging to another owner in the same condominium (owner would still see peers' occurrences on the same condo). Not a data-leak across condos (org+condo filter still applies) but the intent-code is dead. Either remove or complete the fraction ownership check.

operations.py _can_access_document — logic allows any owner-user of the SAME condominium to download documents where related_entity_type is not 'owner' (line 418-419). If sensitive per-owner documents (e.g., another owner's contract, personal ID) are uploaded with only condominium_id set, other owners in that condo would gain access. Consider defaulting new documents' visibility to 'staff-only' or requiring explicit related_entity_id when the category is 'Confidencial'.

operations.py upload_document (line 449) — content_type is trusted from the client (multipart header). Malicious upload with mismatched extension (.exe renamed .pdf) will pass. Consider server-side sniff (python-magic) for high-value categories.
operations.py maintenance FREQ_DAYS uses fixed integers (30/91/182/365) — for 'monthly' this drifts across year (28-31 days). Use dateutil.relativedelta(months=1) for calendar-correct recurrence.

operations.py contract_status — 'active' returned when end_date is None; contracts should probably remain 'draft' or require an end date to become active. Cosmetic but affects dashboard 'contracts_expiring' logic when data is incomplete.

operations.py send_communication — recipient_owner_ids is a list of str but the users query on line 561 does {'owner_id': {'$in': recipient_owner_ids}}; if any owner_id stored in db.users is an ObjectId (schema drift), the $in miss won't notify. Consider unifying id storage as str throughout.
operations.py stores files as base64 in Mongo with MAX_FILE=12MB — for 21+ occurrences × attachments this will bloat working set. Fine for MVP; move to S3/GridFS before scale.

operations.py ops_dashboard iterates db.maintenance and db.contracts in Python to derive status counts — O(N) per call. Use aggregation with $addFields to compute status server-side and $group counts.
